record.paper_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
record.original_question: If primordial multi-universes were in thermal contact inside a thermal bath and were subjected to a contraction crunch before later decoupling, what thermal evolution would our universe inherit from that earlier multiverse interaction?

evidence.quote: There are also questions regarding the multiverse content. For example, the conjuncture of a thermal contact of primordial multi-universes, immersed in a thermal bath, subjected to a contraction crunch, and the thermal evolution consequences to our universe after decoupling.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a primordial ensemble of universes (a "multiverse") that are mutually coupled through thermal contact while immersed in a common thermal bath at some initial temperature T_0. Suppose this ensemble undergoes a contracting (crunch) phase, modeled by a time-dependent scale factor a(t) with da/dt < 0 over a finite interval, during which the constituent universes exchange energy and equilibrate. At a decoupling time t_d, the universes thermally decouple and evolve independently thereafter.

Formulate and determine, within a consistent cosmological framework (for instance, a Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker model coupled to a thermal-bath energy-momentum content together with an inter-universe heat-exchange term), the temperature evolution T(t) inherited by a single member universe (taken to be "our" universe) for t > t_d. In particular:

(a) Specify the equations governing the joint thermodynamic evolution of the multiverse during the contraction phase, including the form of the inter-universe energy exchange and the equation of state of the thermal bath.

(b) Derive the decoupling condition that determines t_d and the post-decoupling initial temperature T(t_d).

(c) Obtain T(t) for t > t_d as a function of the scale factor a(t) of our universe, and identify the observable thermal imprints (if any) on its subsequent expansion history that distinguish this scenario from a universe with no prior multiverse thermal contact.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a speculative open conjecture in a cosmological proposal involving a multiverse with primordial thermal contact and a contraction phase. No standard formulation or resolution of this scenario appears in the literature, and the originating discussion explicitly lists it among open questions. No subsequent works providing a definitive derivation of the inherited thermal evolution were located.

status_evidence.title: Branch-cut cosmology related discussion
status_evidence.snippet: Open questions concerning multiverse thermal contact and post-decoupling consequences are stated as conjectural.
status_evidence.claim: The thermal evolution inherited by our universe from a hypothesized primordial multiverse thermal contact and subsequent contraction crunch remains an unresolved conjectural question.
